f.title: ST&F review practices apply to NDAs, 351(a) BLAs and efficacy supplements
f.statement: The practices and procedures in MAPP 6025.9 apply to NDAs, BLAs submitted under section 351(a) of the PHS Act, and efficacy supplements to those applications. They are intended to improve the quality and consistency of the display of clinical safety data, not the interpretation of these data, in OND reviews of marketing applications.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND, MAPP 6025.9): NDAs, 351(a) BLAs and efficacy supplements; informative for applicants, not binding on them

rows.quote:
The practices and procedures in this MAPP apply to new drug applications (NDAs),
        biologics license applications (BLAs) submitted under section 351(a) of the Public
        Health Service Act (PHS Act), and efficacy supplements to those applications. 1

    •   The procedures in this MAPP are intended to improve the quality and consistency of the
        display of clinical safety data, not interpretation of these data in OND reviews of
        marketing applications.

f.title: ST&F review practices also apply to OTC monograph order requests with clinical trial safety data
f.statement: The ST&F MAPP also applies to over-the-counter monograph order requests (OMORs) where clinical safety data from clinical trials are submitted for FDA to decide whether the drug is generally recognized as safe and effective (GRASE).
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice: OTC monograph order requests with clinical trial safety data submitted for a GRASE determination; informative for requestors

f.statement: Targeted Analysis Guides (TAGs) contain additional analyses used to investigate further safety signals identified during the initial clinical safety review, or certain adverse events of special interest (AESI).

f.title: Customize ST&F example displays to study design, safety issues and emerging issues
f.statement: ST&Fs are a framework for displaying clinical safety data in FDA reviews. The displays are example analyses and should be modified and customized for the specific study design(s), the safety issues, and new issues that arise during the safety evaluation.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND, MAPP 6025.9): NDAs, 351(a) BLAs and efficacy supplements; informative for applicants, not binding on them

f.title: Generate ST&Fs for pivotal trials, other trials of interest and pooled analyses
f.statement: ST&Fs are typically generated for: pivotal or registration trials; any other individual trial of interest to the OND clinical reviewer, including trials that differ substantially from the pivotal trial in key design characteristics (for example lead-in period, enrichment, population, duration, cross-over design); and pooled analyses, if appropriate.
f.applicability: FDA internal review practice (CDER OND, MAPP 6025.9): NDAs, 351(a) BLAs and efficacy supplements; informative for applicants, not binding on them

rows.quote:
ST&Fs are typically generated for the following:

        ‒    Pivotal or registration trials

        ‒    Any other individual trial of interest to the OND clinical reviewer including those that
             differ substantially from the pivotal trial in key design characteristics (e.g., lead-in
             period, enrichment, population, duration, cross-over design)

        ‒    Pooled analyses (if appropriate)

f.title: BIRRS team oversees ST&F development and supports reviewers in safety signal exploration
f.statement: The OND/ODES/DBIRBD Biomedical Informatics and Regulatory Review Science (BIRRS) team, including the Associate Director for Biomedical Informatics (ADBMI), provides program oversight of ST&F development and policies, supports the ST&F Working Group (including member recruitment), and supports the clinical review team in reviewing clinical safety data and exploring safety signals.

        Research, and Biomarker Development (DBIRBD)/Biomedical Informatics and

        ‒   Providing program oversight for ST&Fs development and policies.

        ‒   Supporting the ST&F Working Group, including member recruitment.

f.title: Statistical reviewers shape the ST&F analysis approach, interpret uncertainty and missing data, and run custom analyses
f.statement: The Office of Biostatistics statistical review team contributes to deciding the analysis approach for the ST&Fs for the specific application (given the clinical questions and trial designs), contributes to interpreting clinical safety results (for example statistical uncertainty and the potential impact of missing data), and conducts custom analyses to assess identified signals or AESIs further, where applicable.

        ‒   Contributing to interpretation of clinical safety results (e.g., understanding of
            statistical uncertainty and potential impact of missing data).

        ‒   Conducting custom analyses to further assess identified signals or AESIs, where

f.title: Agree the analytical approach and needed customization before generating the ST&F package
f.statement: Before the ST&F package is generated, the OND CDS team and the cross-disciplinary review team (for example clinical, statistical and ADBMI) together decide the analytical approach for summarizing the clinical safety data in the ST&Fs, and whether customization is needed for the specific trial design(s) and any previously identified review issues, following the ST&F Integrated Guide.

       review team (e.g., clinical, statistical, and ADBMI) work together to:

        a. Determine the analytical approach to summarize the clinical safety data to be
           presented in the ST&Fs.

        b. Determine the need for customization based on the specific trial design(s) and any
           previously identified review issues following the instructions contained within the
           ST&F IG.
